author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can view which veterinarians hold each specialty
summary: A read-only specialty directory lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored name, each with the veterinarians holding it shown by full name (first then last), on a single unpaginated page reachable by its address alone.
acceptance_criteria: Given the clinic's specialties, when the specialty directory is opened, then every specialty is listed by its stored name, each with the veterinarians holding it shown by full name (first name then last name), and all specialties appear on one page
Given a specialty that no veterinarian holds, when the specialty directory is opened, then that specialty is still listed with no veterinarian shown under it
Given a veterinarian who holds no specialty, when the specialty directory is opened, then that veterinarian does not appear on the page
Given the specialty directory, when it is opened, then every specialty renders on a single page and no pagination is offered
non_goals: Managing veterinarians or specialties through the application (NG-2 unchanged)
A navigation entry or inbound link to the page (deferred to a possible follow-up request)
notes: Ordering of specialties and of veterinarians within a specialty is unspecified by the request; narrowest reading is a stable deterministic order, matching the veterinarian directory. See PRD Open Questions.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Extends the established read-only feature-directory pattern (VetController + VetRepository + Thymeleaf template under templates/vets/, system-design §Contracts). Both sanctioning ADRs already cover it: 2026-07-31-server-side-rendering-with-thymeleaf (page render) and 2026-07-31-feature-package-organization (logic in the controller, no service layer), so no new ADR. The one genuinely new mechanic is inverting the unidirectional vet-to-specialty @ManyToMany: Vet owns the association and eagerly fetches its specialties, Specialty carries no back-reference and there is no SpecialtyRepository, so the specialty->vets grouping is computed in SpecialtyController rather than navigated. Added SpecialtyController and updated the VetRepository row in system-design §Contracts.
integration_points: New GET /specialties.html route on a new package-private @Controller in the vet package, mirroring VetController's showVetList

New @Query on VetRepository returning every Specialty ordered by name (JPQL: SELECT s FROM Specialty s ORDER BY s.name) — a derived query cannot be name-derived for Specialty on a Repository<Vet,Integer>, so it is explicit
SpecialtyController injects VetRepository, reads vetRepository.findAll() (eager specialties) plus the new all-specialties query, and builds the specialty->holders grouping
New Thymeleaf template templates/vets/specialtyList.html using the fragments/layout, mirroring vetList.html but with no pagination block
Two message keys reused/added in messages/*.properties for the page heading and any 'none' wording (REQ-LANG-002 requires every key present in every locale)

patterns.description: read-only directory controller: package-private @Controller, GET mapping, Model attribute, view-name return — mirror for showSpecialtyList without the pagination helpers
Vet.getSpecialties() sorts specialties by name; reuse the same stable-ordering intent for both axes of the directory
th:each row rendering vet.firstName + ' ' + vet.lastName is exactly the required full-name form; invert the nesting (outer loop over specialties, inner over holders)

risks.risk: Listing a specialty that no veterinarian holds cannot be derived from the vet graph — the seed data holds all three specialties, so a naive 'collect specialties seen on vets' approach silently passes the seed but violates acceptance criterion 2
risks.mitigation: Drive the specialty list from the all-specialties query (every row of the specialties table), then attach holders; specialties with no holder render with an empty holder list. specialtyDirectoryShouldListEverySpecialtyWithItsVeterinarians must include an unheld specialty in its test data

risks.risk: BaseEntity has identity equality only (no equals/hashCode override), so Specialty instances returned by the all-specialties query and those reached via vet.getSpecialties() are not guaranteed to be the same objects; grouping keyed on Specialty object identity can drop holders
risks.mitigation: Key the grouping on the stored specialty identity or name (getId()/getName()), not on Specialty object identity

risks.risk: Reusing @Cacheable("vets") on the new no-arg specialty query would collide with the existing no-arg findAll() in the same cache region (identical SimpleKey), returning the wrong cached type
risks.mitigation: Leave the specialty query uncached (specialties do not change out of band — NG-2); do not annotate it @Cacheable("vets")

risks.risk: Ordering of specialties and of holders within a specialty is unspecified (PRD Open Questions); an arbitrary DB order is non-deterministic across vendors
risks.mitigation: Narrowest reading — deterministic order: ORDER BY s.name in the query for specialties, and sort holders by last then first name in the controller/template. Matches the vet directory's stable-order intent

notes: No SpecialtyRepository is introduced (PetTypeRepository is the precedent for a lookup-value repository, but file_targets scope the query onto VetRepository and that keeps the surface to the four named files — acceptable, both live in the vet package). Rejected the heavier alternative of adding an inverse @ManyToMany(mappedBy) collection to Specialty: it would change the entity and its fetch semantics for a read-only page and is out of the slice's file_targets. No design-doc-autofix records present since no prior design-block — autofix audit skipped. system-design §Contracts updated (SpecialtyController row added, VetRepository row now cites REQ-SPEC-001).

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: JPQL findSpecialties() is a static, parameterless query (SELECT s FROM Specialty s ORDER BY s.name) — no user input concatenation, not injectable
specialtyList.html renders all user-derived values (specialty name, holder full names) via auto-escaping th:text; no th:utext, inline script, or unescaped sink — no XSS
showSpecialtyList takes no request parameters; there is no attacker-controlled input reaching any sink

Endpoint exposes only the same public directory data (specialty and vet names) as the existing VetController, consistent with the app's unauthenticated read-only directory model — no new trust boundary crossed
No file I/O, deserialization, or new third-party dependencies introduced

author: code-quality-reviewer

findings.description: The th:each loop variable is named `specialty`, so the Specialty record component is accessed as `specialty.specialty.name` — a double-word path that reads as noise to any future reader. The variable name and the record field name collide, making every accessor one level harder to parse.
findings.fix: Rename the loop variable: th:each="sh : ${specialties}" and update all references in the loop body to sh.specialty.name and sh.holders. Alternatively rename the model attribute to `specialtyRows` and the variable to `specialtyRow`.

findings.description: The SpecialtyHolders record's holders component is a mutable ArrayList. Records signal value-object immutability by type, but callers can mutate the list through the accessor. The code-quality checklist requires defensive copies for collections in records. Sorting is applied before construction, so in-constructor mutation is not the risk; downstream mutation after the record escapes buildDirectory() is.
findings.fix: Replace holders.sort(BY_FULL_NAME) and the List constructor argument with List.copyOf(holders.stream().sorted(BY_FULL_NAME).toList()) so the record field is an unmodifiable list.

findings.description: VetController declares its constructor public. SpecialtyController omits the visibility modifier, defaulting to package-private. The class itself is package-private so Spring can inject it, but the inconsistency with the established neighbor pattern is unnecessary.
findings.fix: Add public to the constructor declaration: public SpecialtyController(VetRepository vetRepository).
